title: Authorization, Procurement, and Travel Playbook
author: Jonah Kim
body:
Summary

This playbook consolidates cross-functional procedures for access & permissions, change governance, data stewardship touchpoints, procurement and expense approval, vendor lifecycle controls, and business travel safety. It is a practical companion to policy indexes and a source of templates that teams should reference for day-to-day operations.

Audience and applicability
- Audience: managers, finance approvers, platform and security engineers, procurement specialists, people ops, and program leads.
- Applicability: company-wide for employees, contractors, and third-party vendors when acting on behalf of Redwood Inference or using company funds/systems.

Principles (brief)
- Least privilege and time-limited access.
- Documented approvals with accountable reviewers.
- Risk-based controls: higher security requirements for Restricted data or production infrastructure changes.
- Clear separation of financial authority and technical ownership.

A. Access & Permissions (operational guidance)
1) Core systems & responsibility
- Identity: Okta (SSO) with enforced 2FA and device posture.
- Cloud: GCP IAM for compute/storage and centralized service accounts; Vault for secrets management.
- Owners: each service has a documented owner (team) responsible for entitlement reviews and access policies.

2) Request process (stepwise)
1. Requestor files an Access Request using the Jira template (team-access queue).
2. Manager validates business need and minimal required role.
3. Domain owner (service owner) confirms environment (prod/non-prod) and approves.
4. Security approves for requests involving Restricted data or elevated infra privileges.
5. Provisioning is executed by IT/SRE and recorded with Jira ticket and audit log.

3) Granting rules and expiry
- Default: non-prod environment grants expire in 180 days; prod environment grants expire in 90 days.
- Emergency elevated access: max 7 days with immediate post-incident audit and mandatory justification field.

4) Recertification and audits
- Teams must recertify entitlements quarterly. Security will sample 10% of services monthly and escalate mismatches > 2% to leadership.

B. Change Management (production-facing)
1) Change categories
- Routine: operational maintenance with documented runbook; pre-authorized by service owner.
- Significant: changes that alter model behavior, serving runtime, or infra (requires full change packet).
- Emergency: incident-driven fixes; require retrospective and RCA within 5 business days.

2) Significant change packet must include (single-file checklist)
- Jira ID, owner, rollback plan, monitoring endpoints, and impact window.
- Canary strategy: criteria, traffic percentage, duration, and abort thresholds.
- Load/perf test results and safety eval for model changes (if applicable).

3) Rollout thresholds (recommended defaults)
- Canary: 1-3% traffic for 45-90 minutes. Abort if error rate delta > 0.5% absolute or P95 latency > 30% above baseline.
- Graduated rollout: double allocation every 60-120 minutes after successful validation steps.

C. Data Management highlights
1) Classification: PUBLIC | INTERNAL | SENSITIVE | RESTRICTED. Document examples in the Data Classification appendix.
2) Handling rules
- Restricted: must be stored in VPC-only buckets, encrypted with customer-managed keys, and accessible only by named service accounts.
- Transcripts/PII: apply redaction pipeline before indexing; retain minimal context needed for product features.

3) Retention and deletion
- Default audit logs retention: 365 days. Application telemetry: 90 days unless otherwise approved.
- Data deletion: submit DSR via legal intake; target acknowledgement in 3 business days and completion per regulatory timetable.

D. Procurement & Expenses
1) Approval matrix (summary)
- <$2,000: manager approval.
- $2,000 to $20,000: manager + finance approver.
- >$20,000: manager + finance director + legal review for contract terms.
- Capital equipment (hardware > $10,000) requires procurement + finance capital coding.

2) Preferred process and tools
- Use Procurely portal for PO requests when available. For ad-hoc purchases, attach receipts and PO ID to expense reports in Concur.
- Corporate card policy: allowed for recurring SaaS and vendor subscriptions under $5,000; review monthly card statements for misuse.

3) Contract and vendor spend controls
- Always check vendor index before onboarding new vendors. For vendors with access to Sensitive/Restricted data, require DPA, SOC2/ISO evidence, and security questionnaire.

E. Vendor Management lifecycle (practical steps)
1) Evaluate: initial questionnaire and security review.
2) Contract: include data protection, incident notification within 72 hours, transition assistance, and termination rights.
3) Onboard: assign vendor contact, create inventory entry in vendor registry, set monitoring cadence.
4) Monitor: quarterly health checks for strategic vendors; monthly for operational vendors.
5) Offboard: revoke credentials, confirm data return/deletion, and capture lessons in offboarding ticket.

F. Travel Policy & Safety (condensed)
1) Booking and approvals
- All business travel booked via Concur. Trips with estimated total > $3,500 require director approval and a short travel risk statement for travel to high-risk geographies.

2) Class & accommodations
- Flights: economy for <=6 hours; premium economy/business for >6 hours or medical needs approved by People Ops.
- Hotels: up to $225/night domestic standard; up to $325/night international standard cities (exceptions require approval).

3) Safety and incident handling
- Register itinerary in the People Ops travel tracker. For emergencies, contact People Ops emergency line and use the Global Safety partner. Incidents must be reported within 24 hours.

G. Templates & quick references (links and fields)
- Access request (Jira template): requestor, target service, minimal role, expiration, justification.
- Procurement PO template (Procurely): vendor, SOW/quote, budget code, approvers.
- Vendor security intake: contact info, data types, compliance evidence, required controls.
- Change runbook checklist: rollback, smoke tests, monitoring dashboards, escalation contacts.

H. Roles and owners (concise)
- Finance: owner of procurement rules, per diem schedule, and PO issuance.
- Security: approves elevated access, vendor security intake, and periodic audits.
- Procurement: runs vendor onboarding and contract repository.
- People Ops: onboarding/offboarding coordination and travel safety.
- Engineering teams: own service changes, runbooks, and post-deploy validation.

I. Exceptions and escalations
- Low-risk exceptions: manager + domain owner approval, must include automatic expiry.
- High-risk (production/Restricted data): Security + Finance + Legal sign-off and an executive sponsor. Decision SLA: 3 business days for high-risk exceptions.

J. Reporting and metrics (operational KPIs)
- Monthly dashboards: access request volume, median approval time, open elevated access tickets, number of emergency changes, vendor remediation backlog, and top 10 procurement categories by spend.
- Quarterly audit focus areas: access recertification, active DPAs, high-risk exceptions approved.

Appendices
- Appendix 1: Access decision matrix (examples for SaaS, non-prod, prod).
- Appendix 2: Data classification examples and permitted storage locations.
- Appendix 3: Procurement checklist and sample PO fields.
